title: Bacon Sandwich
subtitle: The perfect British bacon butty
excerpt: Crisp, golden bacon between two slices of soft white bread with butter and your choice of sauce. A British institution that demands attention to the quality of the bacon, the freshness of the bread, and the ratio of all three.

recipe.sourceNotes: The bacon sandwich, or bacon butty, is one of the great British comfort foods and a weekend morning staple. It is the subject of genuine debate: back bacon versus streaky, white bread versus brown, ketchup versus brown sauce, grilled versus fried. The 2007 Oxford University study that allegedly determined the perfect bacon butty formula was widely reported in British press. The correct version is a matter of strong personal conviction, but the fundamentals are shared: good-quality bacon cooked until caramelised.

content.text: Back bacon gives more meat and a familiar British flavour; streaky gives more fat and crispness. Either works. The pan should be hot enough to sizzle immediately when the bacon goes in. Cook the bacon until the fat is caramelised and the edges are slightly crisp; underdone bacon in a sandwich is disappointing. Butter goes on the bread while the bacon is still hot, so it melts in.

Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat. No oil needed. When the pan is hot, add the bacon in a single layer. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side until well caramelised and the fat is golden. The exact time depends on how thick the bacon is.

While the bacon cooks, butter the bread generously. Add the sauce to one slice. When the bacon is ready, lay it on the sauced slice, overlapping the rashers. Close the sandwich and press down firmly. Eat immediately.
